trace.msg: Let's look at this puzzle carefully. I'll only move when I can explain why.
The line must go down: left is number 9, which comes later.
I can't rule out down or left yet, so I'll make an educated guess: down.
Going down leaves no safe move afterwards. So the line goes left.
Going left, the next move is forced and the line gets stuck at cell (3,4); going up, every way of continuing runs into a dead end within a few moves. So the line goes down.
Cell (5,6) has only two exits, so the line must pass through it now: it goes right.
Only one free cell next to the line, so it goes down.
I can't rule out up or left yet, so I'll make an educated guess: up.
Going left, the next 4 moves are forced and the line gets stuck at cell (5,1). So the line goes up.
Going up leaves no safe move afterwards. So the line goes left.
Going down, the next 4 moves are forced and the line gets stuck at cell (5,1). So the line goes up.

Contradiction! Every way forward fails: going up, every way of continuing runs into a dead end within a few moves; going left, the next 2 moves are forced and the line gets stuck at cell (2,3); going right, the next move is forced and the line gets stuck at cell (3,5). So my guess (up from cell (6,4)) was wrong, so the line must go left.
I can't rule out left or up yet, so I'll make an educated guess: left.
Cell (6,1) has only two exits, so the line must pass through it now: it goes left.
Only one free cell next to the line, so it goes up.
Going up, the next 3 moves are forced and the line gets stuck at cell (3,3). So the line goes right.
The line must go right: up is number 7, which comes later.
Going up leaves no safe move afterwards. So the line goes left.
The line must go up: left is number 7, which comes later.
Going left would force the line onto number 7 before its turn; going up, every way of continuing runs into a dead end within a few moves. So the line goes right.
Cell (3,5) has only two exits, so the line must pass through it now: it goes right.
Only one free cell next to the line, so it goes up.
Going up would wall in number 9, the last number. So the line goes left.
Going up would cut off the top-right corner (2 cells). So the line goes left.
Going up would leave both cell (1,1) and cell (1,3) needing the line next, and it can't do both. So the line goes down.
Going left would leave both number 8 and cell (4,1) needing the line next, and it can't do both. So the line goes down.
Only one free cell next to the line, so it goes left.
Every cell is covered and the numbers are in order. Case closed!
